note: Ps70 urgent plea (corrected; near-dup of Ps40:13-17). Human IB: enemies who SEEK (baqash) his life + DELIGHT (chaphets) in his hurt; the God-seekers who SEEK + REJOICE (sus) + GLAD (samach) + LOVE (aheb) God's salvation + magnify him ('God is GREAT'); the psalmist POOR (ani) + NEEDY (ebyon). God-qualifiers=8 (deliver/make-haste/help/salvation/hasten/deliverer/delay) anchored to the needy. Imprecated shame/confusion/dishonor of enemies + superscription = standalone. Every candidate roled.

dims.v: paired with those who delight in his hurt

'Let them be put to shame... who SEEK (baqash) my life' — the murderous hunters; baqash here the enemies' pursuit of the psalmist's life, over against those who seek God (v4) — two kinds of seeking, one deadly, one blessed
delight / take pleasure (chaphets - who delight in my hurt)
paired with those who seek his life

'Let them be turned back... who DELIGHT (chaphets) in my hurt!' — malicious pleasure in another's harm; chaphets here the enemies' relish for the psalmist's ruin - a delight twisted to feed on suffering, the opposite of those who delight in God
issues in rejoicing and gladness in God

'May all who SEEK (baqash) you rejoice and be glad in you!' — the God-seekers, over against those who seek the psalmist's life (v2); baqash here the blessed seeking of God himself, whose reward is joy - the same verb, opposite ends
rejoice / be jubilant (sus - rejoice and be glad in you)
'May all who seek you REJOICE (sus) and be glad in you!' — the joy of the God-seekers; sus here the jubilation of those who find their gladness in God himself, the reward of seeking him
be glad / rejoice (samach - be glad in you)
'rejoice and be GLAD (samach) in you' — the gladness of those who seek God; samach here the joy found not in circumstance but in God, twinned with rejoicing
love (aheb - those who love your salvation)

'May those who LOVE (aheb) your salvation say evermore, God is great!' — devotion to God's saving work; aheb here the love of God's salvation (the qualifier) that overflows in continual praise - loving what God does for the lost
magnify / God is great (gadal - say evermore, God is great)
the praise that flows from loving God's salvation

'say evermore, God is GREAT (gadal)!' — the continual magnifying of God by his lovers; gadal here the God-seekers' ceaseless ascription of greatness to God - worship as a perpetual confession, the fruit of loving his salvation
poor / afflicted (ani - but I am poor and needy)

'But I am POOR (ani) and needy; hasten to me, O God!' — the lowly self-estimate that grounds the plea; ani here the psalmist's affliction and poverty, the very estate God is quick to hear (cf Ps69:33) - weakness owned as the ground of urgent appeal
whom God his help and deliverer must hasten to save (v5)

'I am poor and NEEDY (ebyon); hasten to me, O God! You are my help and my deliverer' — the destitution that casts itself wholly on God; ebyon here the needy psalmist whose only recourse is God his help and deliverer (the qualifiers), pleading he not delay - urgency born of utter dependence
deliver / snatch away (natsal - make haste to deliver me)
God's deliverance the needy psalmist pleads (v1->v5)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's act): 'Make haste, O God, to DELIVER (natsal) me!' - God's rescue is not a human IB char; the deliverance the poor and needy psalmist (282030) urgently pleads. Qualifier.
make haste (chush - make haste to help me)
God's hastening the needy psalmist begs (v1->v5)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'O LORD, MAKE HASTE (chush) to help me!' - God's hastening is not a human IB char; the speed the needy psalmist (282030) begs. Qualifier.
help (ezrah - make haste to help me)
God's help the needy psalmist seeks (v1->v5)
v1 QUALIFIER (God's help): 'make haste to HELP (ezrah) me' - God's help is not a human IB char; the aid the needy psalmist (282030) urgently seeks. Qualifier.
salvation (yeshuah - those who love your salvation)
God's salvation, the object of the God-seekers' love (v4)
v4 QUALIFIER (God's salvation): 'those who love your SALVATION (yeshuah)' - God's saving is not a human IB char; the object of the love that overflows in praise (282022). Qualifier.
make haste (chush - hasten to me, O God)
God asked to hasten to the needy psalmist (v5)
v5 QUALIFIER (God's act asked): 'HASTEN (chush) to me, O God!' - God's hastening is not a human IB char; the speed the needy psalmist (282030) pleads. Qualifier.
God is the needy psalmist's help (v5)
v5 QUALIFIER (God as help): 'You are my HELP (ezer)' - God's being his help is not a human IB char; the aid on which the needy psalmist (282030) depends. Qualifier.
God is the needy psalmist's deliverer (v5)
v5 QUALIFIER (God as deliverer): 'and my DELIVERER (palat)' - God's being his rescuer is not a human IB char; the deliverer the needy psalmist (282030) rests on. Qualifier.
God asked not to delay for the needy psalmist (v5)
v5 QUALIFIER (God's act, negated): 'O LORD, do not DELAY (achar)!' - God's delaying is not a human IB char; the tarrying the needy psalmist (282030) begs him to avoid. Qualifier.
bring to remembrance (zakar - for the memorial offering)
superscription: 'A Psalm of David, for the MEMORIAL OFFERING (zakar)' - the liturgical note in the heading (to bring to remembrance); part of the title. Standalone.
be put to shame (bosh - let them be put to shame)
v2: 'Let them be PUT TO SHAME (bosh)... who seek my life' - the imprecated shame on the enemies; the fate invoked on those who hunt him. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
v2: 'put to shame and CONFUSION (chapher)' - the imprecated confounding of the enemies; twinned with their shame. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
life / soul (nefesh - who seek my life)
v2: 'who seek my LIFE (nefesh)' - the psalmist's life, the object of the enemies' seeking (the char, 282005). Standalone (the life sought).
turn back (sug - let them be turned back)
v2: 'Let them be TURNED BACK (sug)... who delight in my hurt' - the imprecated retreat/repulse of the enemies; the fate invoked. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
v2: 'and BROUGHT TO DISHONOR (kalam)' - the imprecated disgrace of the enemies who delight in his hurt. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
hurt / evil (ra - who delight in my hurt)
v2: 'who delight in my HURT (ra)' - the psalmist's harm, the object of the enemies' malicious delight (the char, 282010). Standalone (the harm).
turn back (shub - let them turn back)
v3: 'Let them turn BACK (shub) because of their shame who say, Aha, Aha!' - the imprecated repulse of the mockers; the fate invoked on those who jeer. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
v3: 'let them turn back because of their SHAME (bosheth)' - the disgrace that repels the mocking enemies; the imprecated shame of those who say 'Aha!'. Standalone (imprecation-fate).
